The test image shows a mango leaf with multiple small, dark brown/reddish-brown spots scattered across the leaf surface. The spots appear discrete, somewhat circular to irregular, and distributed along the leaf. The leaf itself is green and elongated (typical mango leaf shape).

Key visual features:
- Multiple small brown/dark lesions on leaf surface
- Lesions appear raised or slightly sunken with darker centers
- No white powdery coating (rules out Powdery_Mildew)
- No sooty black coating (rules out Sooty_Mould)
- No galls or tissue distortion (rules out Gall_Midge)
- No stem dieback visible (rules out Die_Back)
- No notching/cutting damage on leaf margins (rules out Cutting_Weevil)
- Pattern is consistent with either Anthracnose (dark necrotic lesions) or Bacterial_Canker (water-soaked to brown lesions)

The small, discrete, reddish-brown spots scattered across the leaf surface — without any yellowing halo or water-soaked appearance — are very characteristic of **Anthracnose** on mango. Anthracnose typically causes small dark brown to black lesions on leaves. Bacterial canker tends to produce more angular, water-soaked lesions often with yellow halos.
